claims.statement: For every profile (a2,a3,a4) of nonnegative integers with 1<=m=a2+a3+a4<=99, every represented r in {2,3,4}, and every integer 1<=k<=floor((N+2)/2), the exact zero-extended integer S_r(k)=(h+1)U_r[k]C[k]+(k+1)(h-k+1)(E[k]C[k]-E[k+1]C[k-1]) is positive, where N=2a2+3a3+4a4, h=1+2a2+4a3+7a4, C=(1+2z) product_r B_r^a_r, E=z(1+z)^N, and U_r=(1+2z)B_(r-1)B_r^(a_r-1) product_(s!=r)B_s^a_s. This is a finite bounded-computation claim with no first-descent or selector premise.
claims.scope: Exact finite prefix m=1..99, all represented arities and all guard ranks 1<=k<=floor((N+2)/2), no actual-descent or eligibility filter. It is evidence only for this bounded restriction of E993-PATH-STAR-ARITY-2-4-ULC-EXACT-RATIO-TIP-SURPLUS; it does not prove its all-m scope, the primary selected payment, or any endpoint/weighted/individual comparison.
claims.reason: The frozen exact-integer instrument tested 171699 profiles and 56245000 represented-type/rank rows; every surplus was positive, the minimum was 98, all 99 per-m counts matched the reviewed table, all required controls passed, and the shared transport runner completed without timeout. Finite computation does not establish universal m.

claims.statement: For every nonempty arity-2/3/4 profile with m branches and total N, set beta=2^(N+m+4). Every coefficient of C=(1+2z) product_i B_(r_i) and every coefficient of a represented U_i=(1+2z)B_(r_i-1) product_(l!=i)B_(r_l) is less than beta. Therefore evaluating C and U_i at beta and extracting base-beta digits returns their exact monomial coefficients without carries or cancellation.
claims.scope: All finite nonempty branch profiles with arities 2,3,4; exact coefficient extraction only. This is an implementation lemma and gives no sign result for the surplus or any selected-payment predicate.
claims.reason: At z=1, C(1)=3 product_i(2^r_i+1)<3*2^(N+m)<2^(N+m+2)<beta. Also U_i(1)=3(2^(r_i-1)+1) product_(l!=i)(2^r_l+1)<3*2^(N+m-1)<2^(N+m+1)<beta. Nonnegative coefficients are individually bounded by their coefficient sums. Small exact convolution cross-checks passed.

limitations: The computation covers only m<=99; the all-m surplus requires the separately reviewed m>=100 tail and its proof dependencies.
The tested surplus has no actual first-descent or strict-selector filter. It does not establish the primary selected payment, selected MASS, guarded comparisons, endpoint bridge, or Erdős993.
This is bounded computation and informal implementation reasoning, not a Lean award or a universal status promotion.
